title: The Last Ledger Revisited
premise: Bram Voss, the nonbinary archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a murder in the cathedral's sealed crypt forty years ago, and one promising a second death before the trial opens. As police fixate on the wrong suspect, Bram discovers that the cathedral's ancient donation ledger conceals a coded record of payments, favors, and silences kept by generations of churchwardens. Decoding it pulls Bram into an uneasy alliance with the accused man's estranged daughter and a retired detective who once buried the case. The ledger's final entry names the true killer — the cathedral's beloved dean — who has been quietly eliminating everyone who could read it. In the crypt on the eve of trial, Bram confronts him, survives an attempt on their life, and chooses justice over the institution they love, testifying as the ledger is entered into evidence.
about_author: Jonah Winterbourne is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to reread. They write mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside institutions.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Bram Voss sorts the morning post in the archive loft and finds two letters: a detailed confession to a 1984 killing in the locked crypt, and a second note promising 'one more before the gavel.' Both are written in the same careful hand. POV: Bram. Beat: unease — the archivist realizes the past has just knocked.

chapters.title: The Crypt That Isn't Empty
chapters.summary: Bram descends to the sealed crypt against protocol and finds fresh candle wax beside a coffin untouched for decades. Detective Inspector Sera Okonkwo arrives, skeptical but rattled; the confession letter matches details never made public. POV: Bram. Beat: dread deepening into obligation.

chapters.title: The Man in the Dock Already
chapters.summary: Police arrest Tomas Reyes, a former verger with a grudge, on thin circumstantial evidence. His daughter Lucía storms into the archive demanding records that might clear him. Bram, bound by duty, initially refuses her. POV: Bram. Beat: conflict between institutional loyalty and conscience.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Cataloguing the churchwardens' donation ledger, Bram notices columns of figures that don't balance — recurring sums annotated with tiny symbols matching the confession letter's watermark. Someone encoded a second book inside the first. POV: Bram. Beat: the thrill of the hunt cutting through fear.

chapters.title: What the Dean Knew
chapters.summary: Dean Ambrose Fenn warmly warns Bram off 'digging up bones,' offering a promotion instead. Bram accepts graciously and lies awake replaying every kindness Fenn has shown them over ten years. POV: Bram. Beat: love against duty begins its quiet war.

chapters.title: Lucía's Key
chapters.summary: Lucía returns with her father's old keyring; one brass key fits the crypt's secondary door. She reveals Tomas confessed to her years ago — not to murder, but to witnessing one and being paid to forget. POV: alternating Bram/Lucía. Beat: found family sparks between two guarded strangers.

chapters.title: The Cipher of Tithes
chapters.summary: Working nights, Bram cracks the ledger's system: amounts encode initials, dates, and payments. The 1984 entry lists four recipients — three now dead, one still living at the cathedral. POV: Bram. Beat: triumph shadowed by the realization that decoding makes Bram a target.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Reading Room
chapters.summary: A small fire destroys the archive's loan register the night after Bram photographs the ledger pages. The fire brigade calls it faulty wiring; Bram knows better. POV: Bram. Beat: fear arrives — this is no longer research but survival.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Cold File
chapters.summary: Retired detective Marcus Hale, who worked the original 1984 case, contacts Bram through Lucía. He admits he was ordered to close the file and has hated himself since. He gives Bram the victim's name: Elspeth Marr, a young organist. POV: Hale. Beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Elspeth's Music
chapters.summary: Bram traces Elspeth Marr through choir records: brilliant, beloved, and abruptly erased from every program after her death. Her surviving brother confirms she'd discovered financial irregularities. POV: Bram. Beat: grief for a stranger becoming personal resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: A third letter reaches Bram directly: 'You read faster than the others. One more before the gavel.' The handwriting matches both originals. Bram must decide whether to tell Okonkwo everything or protect the ledger from seizure. POV: Bram. Beat: isolation — trust is now a liability.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Bram and Lucía meet secretly to compare notes and are nearly caught by the night watchman. In the scramble, Lucía is injured; Bram carries her out, and their alliance hardens into something like kinship. POV: Bram. Beat: found family cemented under pressure.

chapters.title: The Living Name
chapters.summary: The decoded ledger's final living recipient is revealed by initials only: A.F. Bram refuses to believe it means Dean Fenn and hunts for another reading. There isn't one. POV: Bram. Beat: heartbreak — the mentor is the monster.

chapters.title: Confession of a Watchman
chapters.summary: The night watchman, terrified, tells Bram he was paid for years to leave the crypt door unlocked on certain anniversaries — always by the dean's office. Then he vanishes before he can sign a statement. POV: Bram. Beat: mounting horror as witnesses evaporate.

chapters.title: Hale Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Hale formally recants his 1984 closure report to Okonkwo, exposing the old cover-up and burning his pension and reputation. Okonkwo, cornered between career and conscience, agrees to reopen the case quietly. POV: Hale/Okonkwo. Beat: justice outside the law takes institutional form.

chapters.title: The Trial Opens
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes stands trial amid media frenzy. Fenn testifies beautifully for the prosecution, serene and devastating. Watching from the gallery, Bram sees how easily the truth will lose. POV: Bram. Beat: despair at the machinery of respectable lies.

chapters.title: One More Before the Gavel
chapters.summary: Lucía disappears. A fourth letter arrives: the promised 'one more' has been taken, not killed — yet. Bram decodes a final ledger annotation pointing to the crypt and understands where Fenn keeps what he cannot destroy. POV: Bram. Beat: terror transmuted into desperate courage.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Bram enters the crypt alone at night, ledger photographs hidden in their coat, and finds Lucía alive but drugged among the coffins — alongside boxes of forty years of hush-money records. Fenn steps out of the dark holding a lantern. POV: Bram. Beat: the confrontation begins.

chapters.title: The Dean's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Fenn explains, calm and almost tender: Elspeth died because she would have ruined the cathedral, and every payment since was stewardship. He offers Bram the same choice Tomas got — silence, salary, belonging. POV: Bram/Fenn. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Bram Refuses
chapters.summary: Bram answers with the truth: a cathedral is its people, not its stones, and Elspeth was one of its people. When Fenn moves toward them, Okonkwo and Hale — tipped by a coded message Bram left in the ledger itself — flood down the stairwell. POV: Bram. Beat: climax; refusal becomes rescue.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: The trial collapses and reopens around the ledger, Hale's recantation, and Bram's testimony. Fenn is convicted; Tomas is freed. Bram reads Elspeth's name aloud in court so the record finally holds it. POV: Bram. Beat: catharsis — justice spoken plainly.

chapters.title: A New Entry in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Months later, Bram catalogs the cleaned-out crypt, adds a memorial plaque for Elspeth, and shares Sunday supper with Lucía, Tomas, Hale, and Okonkwo — a strange new family. The last line of the ledger, in Bram's hand, simply records the truth. POV: Bram. Beat: resolution; the archive keeper writes themselves into the record.
